intent: Share the open delay across every tooltip in a subtree and group them, so once one opens its neighbours open instantly.
typical_uses: A toolbar or icon rail whose triggers all carry tooltips
Once near the application root, grouping every tooltip below it

dont_use_when.situation: A tooltip that should keep the primitive's standard hover delay

instead.note: Mount the Tooltip without a provider around it; inside one, the kit's default provider delay of 0 opens it with no wait.

invariants.text: TooltipProvider renders no DOM element; it only provides context to every Tooltip below it.

Left at its default `delay` of 0, every tooltip inside opens with no wait and a TooltipTrigger's own `delay` is ignored; with a non-zero `delay` here, a trigger's own `delay` takes precedence over it.
Once one tooltip inside has opened, another one opened within `timeout` milliseconds of the previous closing opens with no delay and without its open transition.

anti_patterns.dont: Wrap each Tooltip in its own TooltipProvider
anti_patterns.do_instead: Wrap the whole group in one provider - each tooltip joins the nearest provider above it, so separate providers form separate groups

children.states: children is any React content; every Tooltip inside it, at any depth, joins the group
children.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

good.title: A toolbar whose tooltips open as a group
A group that waits before its first tooltip opens

bad.title: A per-trigger delay expected to slow a default provider
bad.why: Under a provider at its default delay of 0 the trigger's own `delay` is ignored and the tooltip opens with no wait; set `delay` on the provider instead.

children.description: TS: ReactNode. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. children is any React content; every Tooltip inside it, at any depth, joins the group. `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.
